figures.caption: Threshold voltage VT0 versus channel length L. The data are from measurements of a single site on a wafer, so include local statistical variation.
Threshold voltage VT0 versus channel length L from a physically based model. Notice the smoothness and monotonicity of the model.
Measured drain current (ID, solid lines) and output conductance (gdd, dash lines, dot-dash is where gdd < 0) from a typical LDMOS transistor.
Normalized resistance R versus width W for an integrated resistor. The curves, from top to bottom, are for high, typical, and low resistance process corners, respectively.
Resistor conductance 1/R versus width W showing correct and incorrect asymptotic behavior.
Measured output conductance (normalized to the low-frequency value) as a function of frequency for a FinFET (go = gdd) and a SiGe HBT (go = gcc). The frequency dependence is from self-heating.

Simulation of a simple inverter (with a resistive load) using BSIM4. The 'spike' for xpart = 0 is from lack of modeling of NQS behavior. The xpart = 1 'correction' ameliorates the unphysical spike, but messes up capacitance modeling.
